payload.comment: The architecture_research stage is internally consistent and well-grounded for the 28×28 RGB PathMNIST task (9-class, ~90k train, 1.63:1 imbalance). Key strengths: (1) Correct identification of H&E channel asymmetry (green std 0.177 vs red/blue ~0.124) and appropriate per-channel standardization; (2) Reasonable architecture priority ordering (compact_transformer → resnet18 → residual_cnn → vision_transformer → tiny_cnn) appropriate for the data scale; (3) Sound parametrization guidance (width 192–384, depth 4–6, heads 4–6) with appropriate regularization (stochastic depth, weight decay, label smoothing); (4) Conv tokenization with stride 4 (49 tokens) as primary is well-justified for preserving nuclear morphology at 28×28; (5) All augmentations in the representation plan (hflip, brightness, rotate90) are built-in primitives requiring no extension approval. Minor notes: (a) The extension_gate_report lists tissue_geometric_aug (hflip/vflip) as pending_review, which is redundant since these are built-in augmentations that do not require approval—harmless but adds unnecessary gate overhead; (b) compact_conv_stem_transformer remains pending_review in the extension gate; the architecture research references it as a binding proposal, which is acceptable at the research/analysis stage but implementation will require gate clearance; (c) The stride inconsistency between the idea (stride 7) and the binding proposal (stride 4) is correctly resolved in favor of the proposal and noted as a traceability item only; (d) llm_model_digest is null for qwen3.8, a minor reproducibility gap for LLM-assisted analysis. No deterministic findings are present. The risk assessment is thorough and appropriately calibrated (overfitting boundary at 90k samples, binary stride granularity, channel-specific augmentation sensitivity). The evidence sources (arXiv 2010.11929, 2104.05704, 2110.14795) are relevant to compact transformer and conv-tokenization design. Proceed to next stage.
